query: Which university did the inventor of the World Wide Web study at?
answer: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web, and he studied at the University of Oxford. He was at The Queen's College, Oxford, from 1973 to 1976 and graduated with a first-class degree in physics [1][2]. While he was there, he built a computer out of spare parts, including an old television. He was also caught hacking and banned from using the university's computers [2][3].
